title: Redwood - Security BCDR & Incident Response Review - Northbridge Bank
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood), Rajiv (Northbridge), Elena (Northbridge CISO), Marcus (SRE), Sofia (Cloud Ops)

Summary: quick security and BCDR deep-dive focusing on incident response timelines (RTO/RPO), uptime/SLA targets and the escalation process. Customer asked about audit log retention, KMS encryption, RBAC/SSO and SOC2/ISO evidence.

Topics: BCDR / IR runbooks; RTO/RPO expectations; SLA (uptime, credits); escalation path (PagerDuty, engineering on-call, Redwood CISO); encryption/KMS key management; audit logs and retention; SSO/SAML and RBAC role mappings; SOC 2 / ISO evidence sharing.

00:00:05 - Samira: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. we're going to go through incident response and b c d r, and then cover a few items elena flagged in the security questionnaire.
00:00:13 - Rajiv: thanks, samira. we wanted to confirm our rto needs — we target 15 minutes for full service impact detection to mitigation on our end, and rpo of 5 minutes for critical token data flows.
00:00:25 - Liam: got it, yeah. quick note — our hosted api typically meets a 99.95% uptime SLA and we have defined rto/rpo commitments for dedicated/private options, the latter can be tuned by retention of standby capacity and cross-region failover.
00:00:40 - Elena: 99.95 is fine as a baseline, but for high value payment flows we might need 99.99 or guaranteed failover in 5 minutes. what's the typical failover story?
00:00:52 - Priya: so for private and dedicated we've got cross-region replication for metadata and model state, kv cache warmup strategies, and an automated failover policy that can route traffic to warm replicas. warming time depends on sequence length and kv warming, usually 3-10 minutes but we can instrument aggressive pre-warm for SLAs closer to 5.
00:01:10 - Marcus: can you clarify the warming step — is that warming the kv cache or spinning up new gpus? we can't afford long cold starts.
00:01:18 - Liam: both can be involved. we maintain a buffer of pre-provisioned instances in dedicated pools; when you choose a high-availability profile we keep a minimal set of warm workers plus a pre-warmed kv cache snapshot. cold start to full throughput is what causes the 3-10 minute window. on private installs you can also opt for always-on nodes.
00:01:39 - Sofia: how do you define rpo for models? are you snapshotting kv caches or just input data?
00:01:45 - Priya: RPO is measured for customer request/ingress data (logs, payloads) — we persist those in encrypted blobstore with configurable replication. model state (kv cache) is best-effort to reduce latency on failover; we have optional continuous replication of checkpointed states for enterprise customers to achieve sub-5 minute rpo for inference context.
00:02:06 - Rajiv: ok, what's the incident escalation process? we need names, SLAs for initial response, and postmortem cadence.
00:02:12 - Liam: primary on-call detection is via Redwood infra monitoring tied to metrics and alerting; alerts create PagerDuty incidents immediately for Sev1. initial acknowledgement target is 5 minutes for Sev1, engineer triage within 15, and mitigation steps within 60 by default. we also have a dedicated cs/cse war room for major incidents.
00:02:31 - Elena: is PagerDuty integration standard? and can we map to our on-call?
00:02:36 - Samira: yes, PD integration is standard; we support escalation rules to forward to your on-call rotations and you can configure runbooks to auto-assign.
00:02:44 - Marcus: what about audit logging — we need immutable logs for 1 year, ideally 3 years, with tamper evidence and export to our SIEM.
00:02:52 - Priya: audit logs are captured at the control plane and data plane — API requests, admin actions, and config changes. retention is configurable; exports to S3 or your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/ELK) are supported. we provide signed log bundles for tamper-evidence and an append-only store option for long-term retention.
00:03:15 - Elena: encryption questions — do you use customer-managed keys? how's KMS integration done?
00:03:20 - Liam: support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault. keys can be rotated on customer cadence; for private deployments the HSM/KMS sits inside your VPC or on-prem HSM. we can provide proof of key separation and key usage logs.
00:03:37 - Rajiv: does Redwood ever have access to plaintext user payloads?
00:03:40 - Priya: by default Redwood processes inputs for inference in memory, not stored in plaintext; logs and blobs are encrypted at rest. with customer-managed keys we cannot decrypt without your keys. we also offer options to mask or strip PII before persistence.
00:03:54 - Sofia: compliance evidence — we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts, plus recent penetration test results.
00:03:59 - Samira: we can share SOC 2 / ISO reports under NDA via our secure portal; penetration test summaries and redacted findings are available as well.
00:04:10 - Elena: on RBAC and SSO — can we bind roles to our IdP groups, and support SCIM provisioning?
00:04:15 - Liam: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM user provisioning is supported; we map IdP groups to RBAC roles (admin, ops, read-only, audit). fine-grained API roles exist and you can create custom roles for environment-level access.
00:04:29 - Marcus: what's in the runbook? do you provide playbooks for a degraded model quality incident vs full outage?
00:04:35 - Priya: we have separate runbooks — quality regression runbook (roll back to previous model snapshot, run evals, promote stable model) and outage runbook (failover to replica region, activate circuit-breaker and route to lower-cost model variants). we can include your team in rehearsals and tabletop exercises.
00:04:52 - Rajiv: tabletop exercises sound good. frequency?
00:04:54 - Samira: quarterly for critical customers, annual optionally; we recommend quarterly for payment flows.
00:04:59 - Elena: SLA credits — if you miss 99.95 we need defined credits and blackout windows during planned maint.
00:05:05 - Liam: SLA credits are tiered. for hosted API, 99.95 monthly uptime is baseline; credits escalate if below thresholds (e.g., 99.9, 99.0). planned maintenance windows are communicated 72 hours in advance and don't count toward SLA. for Dedicated/Private we can negotiate stricter SLAs in contract.
00:05:25 - Sofia: do you support data residency and region-locked deployments?
00:05:29 - Priya: yes — we support region locking, and private deployments can be fully air-gapped. audit trails and logs remain in-region per configuration.
00:05:37 - Rajiv: what's your mean time to restore historically for Sev1 incidents?
00:05:41 - Liam: median mttr for Sev1 last year was ~28 minutes across hosted incidents; dedicated customers with warm failover saw medians of 12-16 minutes.
00:05:51 - Elena: do you publish incident postmortems?
00:05:53 - Samira: we publish high level postmortems for platform-wide incidents; for customer-impacting incidents we provide a redwood-customer-specific postmortem and internal timeline with action items under NDA.
00:06:02 - Rajiv: curious about to what degree you runbooks are editable by us — can we author steps?
00:06:07 - Priya: yes, we can share editable runbooks (markdown or confluence) and show you how to integrate your contact points and automations.
00:06:15 - Marcus: what's your monitoring stack and how do you do detection? we use synthetic checks and anomaly detection.
00:06:20 - Liam: infra uses Prometheus + Grafana, synthetic canaries, distributed tracing, plus ML-based anomaly detection for token-level latency deviations. alerts are integrated to PD. you can feed your own telemetry to our dashboard for combined views.
00:06:33 - Elena: legal asks around breach notification timelines — what's your SLA for notification to customers?
00:06:38 - Samira: for confirmed breaches we notify customers within 72 hours; for incidents impacting customer data confidentiality we aim for immediate notification and a 24-hour initial update. contractual terms can be tightened.
00:06:51 - Rajiv: we need to validate the escalation matrix — can you show names and roles of folks who would be involved?
00:06:58 - Liam: high level: first responder (on-call engineer), shift lead, SE/architecture lead, product & security lead, Redwood CISO. we can provide contact routing and on-call rotation summaries as part of the security pack.
00:07:10 - Sofia: do you use encrypted comms for escalation? such as dedicated secure channels?
00:07:14 - Priya: we can provision private slack channels and encrypted war rooms; we also support phone bridges and O365 teams.
00:07:21 - Marcus: any gotchas on private/on-prem installs — eg network setup to allow health checks without exposing control plane?
00:07:28 - Liam: control plane connectivity can be configured via private link, or via customer-VPN, or air-gapped with manual sync. we recommend private-link with narrow IP allow-listing and mTLS for health checks.
00:07:41 - Rajiv: audit logs—can you provide schema and sample entries?
00:07:44 - Priya: yes, we'll include sample log schema in the artifact bundle; it includes timestamp, actor, action, resource, request-id, trace-id, region, and signed-hash for tamper-evidence.
00:07:58 - Elena: for SOC2 report sharing, what's the process?
00:08:02 - Samira: NDA first, then share via our secure portal. we usually sign an abbreviated NDA and provide a time-limited download.
00:08:10 - Rajiv: ok next — incident replay and forensic access. can we get log exports as part of forensics?
00:08:15 - Priya: yes, full audit log exports, network flow logs, and available traces. forensics packages are delivered under an evidence transfer workflow.
00:08:26 - Sofia: are backups encrypted separately from primary? CAAS?
00:08:30 - Liam: backups are encrypted with the same KMS options and stored with replication; we also support immutable snapshot storage for longer retention windows.
00:08:40 - Marcus: do you have a defined RTO/RPO table for each deployment mode we can embed in our risk register?
00:08:46 - Priya: yes — we'll provide a table: Hosted API (RTO 15-60m, RPO 5-15m), Dedicated (RTO 5-20m with warm failover, RPO 1-5m with continuous replication), Private (configurable to sub-5m with always-on nodes). we'll include best practices and cost tradeoffs.
00:09:05 - Rajiv: can we request a pilot that includes a simulated failover drill?
00:09:08 - Samira: absolutely — we can schedule a 2-week pilot with a one-day failover exercise and a follow-up retro.
00:09:15 - Elena: small nit — do you keep PII in logs by default? we need pseudonymization.
00:09:20 - Priya: default is to minimize PII and we offer request-level masking; you can enable strict PII redaction at ingestion.
00:09:28 - Marcus: mention of competitor — we evaluated BigCloudAI and SelfHostX, curious about differences in SLA and tooling.
00:09:35 - Samira: we differentiate on observability and developer ergonomics; our Optimize tooling gives model/quantization recommendations tied to cost.
00:09:43 - Rajiv: ok, let's talk deliverables and timeline.
00:09:46 - Liam: we'll send the security artifact bundle (SOC2/ISO samples, runbooks, log schema), a proposed RTO/RPO table, and a pilot scope including a failover drill.
00:09:57 - Samira: i'll follow up with pricing for dedicated warm pools and the pilot estimate.
00:10:02 - Elena: can you include a sample postmortem template and any redacted incident timelines?
00:10:06 - Priya: yes, included in the bundle.
00:10:10 - Rajiv: good. any other questions?
00:10:13 - Sofia: one more — licensing for private deploy, is there an enterprise contract template?
00:10:17 - Samira: we can share an enterprise term sheet; we'll mark redlines for security and data residency clauses.
00:10:24 - Marcus: ok thanks, we've got what we need for now.
00:10:27 - Samira: quick recap then next steps.
00:10:30 - Samira: recap: 1) security artifact bundle (SOC2/ISO/pen test summaries + log schema + runbooks) 2) RTO/RPO table per deployment mode 3) pilot proposal with failover drill 4) pricing for dedicated warm pools and SLA options 5) sample postmortem template and editable runbooks.
00:10:50 - Rajiv: good, timeline? we want the bundle and pilot scope by next wed.
00:10:55 - Samira: we'll aim to deliver by next wednesday.
00:10:58 - Elena: thanks everyone.
00:11:00 - Meeting continues with administrative clarifications and small interruptions (laughter, cross talk).

[transcription notes: occasional mis-heard acronyms — e.g., k v cache vs k v cash in transcript; minor filler words. timestamps approximate. some speaker labels simplified.]
summary: Customer and Redwood reviewed incident response/BCDR expectations: RTO/RPO, SLA tiers (99.95 vs 99.99), failover strategies, PagerDuty integration, audit logs & retention, KMS/customer-managed keys, SOC2/ISO evidence sharing, RBAC/SSO/SCIM, runbooks and tabletop exercises. Agreed deliverables: security artifact bundle, RTO/RPO table, pilot with failover drill, pricing for dedicated warm pools, postmortem template.
